## Context Mode usage

When reading large files, MCP results, or web fetches:

- For files > 5 KB: use Context Mode index + search tools (`ctx_index` / `ctx_search` or host-qualified MCP names) instead of reading the whole file.
- For Playwright snapshots, web fetches, and other MCP tool results: use `ctx_execute` to run a sandboxed script that processes the result and only returns relevant `console.log` lines.
- For batch reads (5+ files): use `ctx_batch_execute` instead of N separate reads.

If a call returns "tool not found", run Context Mode doctor in a live session to confirm the exact tool prefix for your host, or use slash commands where available (`/ctx-index`, `/ctx-search` on Claude Code).

For everything else, use your normal tools. RTK handles shell command output automatically when RTK is opted in and wired.

## Project Overview

Silver Bullet is a host-aware plugin — an agentic process orchestrator that enforces structured AI-native workflows via hooks, skills, and a state machine. It ships as a plugin (installed via `/plugin install` or the `alo-labs/agent-plugins` marketplace) and activates inside any downstream project.

- **Stack**: Bash (hooks, lib, scripts, tests), Python (generators, validators, hook payload helpers, coverage tooling), Markdown (skills, templates, docs), JSON (config, manifests)
- **Git repo**: https://github.com/alo-exp/silver-bullet.git
- **Runtime prerequisites**: `bash`, `jq`, `git`, `python3`; `gh` for the CI and release gates. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md#prerequisites) for the contributor tool list.

> **Development rule**: All code edits go to **source files in this repo** (`hooks/`, `scripts/`, `skills/`, `templates/`, `tests/`, `.github/`, etc.). Never modify the installed plugin cache at the host's plugin cache path (for example `${SB_RUNTIME_HOME_ROOT}/plugins/cache/alo-labs/silver-bullet/*/` or the equivalent Codex cache path) — that is a read-only build artifact. Source changes here are what gets released and installed.

## Commands

### Running Tests

```bash
# Makefile entry points (each wraps the script commands below)
make setup        # prerequisite check + python3 -m pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
make check        # make lint + make test: what a pull request must pass
make coverage     # Bash, Python and JS/TS coverage (FAIL_UNDER=N for a threshold)

# Every default suite: hooks, scripts (including tests/python and tests/js through
# test-python-unit.sh / test-js-unit.sh), integration, harness, docs, e2e-live harness,
# TUI contracts, then the hook coverage matrix
bash tests/run-all-tests.sh
bash tests/run-all-tests.sh --jobs 4          # parallel
bash tests/run-all-tests.sh --suite docs      # suites whose directory matches
bash tests/run-all-tests.sh --list            # list test files only

# Single test files (directly, or through the runner for the sandboxed HOME)
bash tests/hooks/test-completion-audit.sh
bash tests/run-all-tests.sh tests/integration/test-e2e-enforcement-gates.sh

# Coverage (python3 -m pip install -r requirements-dev.txt first)
bash tests/coverage/run-coverage.sh
```

See [docs/TESTING.md](docs/TESTING.md) for the layout, isolation and live suites.

### Linting and Validation

```bash
# Syntax-check all hook and script files
for f in hooks/*.sh hooks/lib/*.sh scripts/*.sh; do bash -n "$f" || echo "FAIL: $f"; done

# ShellCheck as CI runs it: application Bash at every severity, tests at -S warning
# (make lint runs this plus bash -n and jq; any finding fails)
bash scripts/lint-shell.sh --all

# Repository invariants (manifests, versions, hook references, skill lists, mirrors)
bash scripts/check-repo-invariants.sh

# JSON validity
jq . hooks/hooks.json > /dev/null && echo "hooks.json valid"
jq . .silver-bullet.json > /dev/null && echo ".silver-bullet.json valid"
jq . templates/silver-bullet.config.json.default > /dev/null

# Generated files are current
python3 scripts/generate-hook-reference.py --check
python3 scripts/generate-apo-artifacts.py --check
bash scripts/validate-plugin-mirror.sh
```

### Development Setup (for contributors)

[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md#development-setup) has the macOS and Linux setup. In the host coding agent, `/sb:init` activates enforcement in this repo.

## Architecture

### Core Concepts

Silver Bullet has **two personas**:
1. **As a plugin** — installs into end-user projects. Users never see the source; they interact with `silver-bullet.md` (and an existing `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md`, which `/sb:init` reconciles in place) generated by `/sb:init`.
2. **As a repo** — this codebase, where enforcement is active on itself (dogfooding).

The three pillars:

| Pillar | Location | Role |
|--------|----------|------|
| **Skills** | `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` | Orchestrator instructions loaded by the Skill tool |
| **Hooks** | `hooks/*.sh`, `hooks/session-start` + `hooks/hooks.json` | Runtime enforcement injected into every host coding session |
| **Config** | `.silver-bullet.json` (per-project) + `templates/silver-bullet.config.json.default` | Required-skill lists, state file paths, src patterns |

### Hook Architecture

`hooks/hooks.json` registers 96 hook commands backed by 64 hook scripts on seven events: SessionStart, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, SubagentStart, Stop, SubagentStop and UserPromptSubmit. None is async. **[docs/HOOKS.md](docs/HOOKS.md) is the complete reference** (event, matcher, timeout and purpose of every hook); it is generated by `scripts/generate-hook-reference.py`, and `tests/docs/test-hook-reference.sh` fails when it is stale. In outline:

- **SessionStart** — `session-start` injects the core rules (`hooks/core-rules.md`) and resets branch-scoped state; `spec-session-record.sh`, `stack-compression-lifecycle.sh`, `rfl-quota-retry-due.sh`.
- **PreToolUse** — matchers cover both Claude and Codex tool names (`Bash|exec_command`, `Edit|Write|MultiEdit|apply_patch`, `Skill`, `Task|Subagent|Agent`, `Read|Grep`, `WebFetch`, MCP). Main gates: `dev-cycle-check.sh` and `workflow-chain-guard.sh` (planning floor), `completion-audit.sh` (delivery floors), `ci-status-check.sh`, `planning-file-guard.sh`, `roadmap-freshness.sh`, `phase-archive.sh`, `spec-floor-check.sh`, `forbidden-skill-check.sh`, `uat-gate.sh`, the orchestrator guards, site-session guards and the opt-in tool gates.
- **PostToolUse** — recorders (`record-skill.sh` and the other `record-*.sh`), `dev-cycle-check.sh`, `completion-audit.sh` and `ci-status-check.sh` again (post-command checks and warnings), `compliance-status.sh` (informational), `trivial-file-clear.sh`, `pr-traceability.sh`, `session-log-init.sh`, `timeout-check.sh`, `semantic-compress.sh`, `flow-advance.sh`.
- **Stop / SubagentStop** — `stop-check.sh` (planning floor) plus `outcomes-check.sh`, `instruction-ledger-gate.sh`, site gates, `subagent-stop-enforcement.sh` and `phase-lock-release.sh`.
- **UserPromptSubmit** — `record-requested-skill.sh`, `prompt-reminder.sh`, `outcomes-check.sh`, `instruction-ledger-gate.sh` and others.

Cursor uses `hooks/cursor-hooks.json`, generated from `hooks/hooks.json` by `scripts/generate-cursor-hooks.py` and wrapped by `hooks/cursor-hook-bridge.sh`; the Codex installer routes hooks through `hooks/codex-hook-adapter.sh`.

### Two-Tier Enforcement Model

`completion-audit.sh` and `stop-check.sh` enforce two separate gates:

1. **Intermediate commits** (`git commit`, `git push`, and git plumbing that creates commits: `write-tree`, `commit-tree`, `hash-object -w`, `update-ref refs/heads/*`) and **Stop** — require only the `required_planning` skills (default: `silver-quality-gates`, `silver-context`, `silver-plan`; `required_planning_devops` in the DevOps workflow). This lets execution subagents make atomic commits mid-execution.
2. **Final delivery** (`gh pr create`, `gh pr merge`, a command whose first line contains the word `deploy`, `gh release create`) — requires the full `required_deploy` list from `.silver-bullet.json`; `gh release create` also needs `required_release` and the configured release gates.

Default skill lists come from `templates/silver-bullet.config.json.default`. Hooks source `hooks/lib/required-skills.sh`, which reads that file with `jq` at runtime; the project's `.silver-bullet.json` lists take precedence when present.

### State Machine

Skill invocations are recorded to `${SB_RUNTIME_HOME_ROOT}/.silver-bullet/state` by `record-skill.sh` (on `PostToolUse` for the Skill tool, and for `silver-bullet invoke-skill` receipts on Codex). The state is:
- **Branch-scoped**: wiped when `git branch` or git worktree toplevel changes between sessions (tracked via `${SB_RUNTIME_HOME_ROOT}/.silver-bullet/branch`)
- **Trivial bypass (legacy)**: if `${SB_RUNTIME_HOME_ROOT}/.silver-bullet/trivial` exists (real file, not symlink), the gates that source `hooks/lib/trivial-bypass.sh` exit 0. `session-start` deletes the marker, `trivial-file-clear.sh` deletes it after any file write, and `trivial-file-guard.sh` blocks agents from creating it; small changes go through `/sb:fast` instead.

### SB OVERRIDE (audited escape hatch)

When a blocking orchestrator directive cannot be satisfied, include in your next user message:

`SB OVERRIDE: <reason>`

The hook logs the override to `.planning/orchestrator-override-log.jsonl` and clears the pending directive. Documented in `silver-bullet.md` §2h and `docs/ORCHESTRATOR.md`.

**Test env-var overrides** (mirrors the `SILVER_BULLET_STATE_FILE` pattern):
- `SILVER_BULLET_STATE_FILE` — overrides the default state file path (`${SB_RUNTIME_HOME_ROOT}/.silver-bullet/state`); must remain under `${SB_RUNTIME_HOME_ROOT}/`
- `SILVER_BULLET_BRANCH_FILE` — overrides the branch-tracking file path (`${SB_RUNTIME_HOME_ROOT}/.silver-bullet/branch`); must remain under `${SB_RUNTIME_HOME_ROOT}/`. Used by integration tests (`tests/integration/helpers/common.sh`) to supply a per-test mock branch file so `session-start` does not read or mutate the live branch file during test runs.

### Shared Libraries (`hooks/lib/`)

`hooks/lib/` holds about sixty sourced helpers; none is registered as a hook. [docs/HOOKS.md](docs/HOOKS.md#shared-libraries-hookslib) lists every file by group. The ones most hooks depend on:

| Group | Files | Role |
|-------|-------|------|
| Runtime and plumbing | `runtime-paths.sh`, `hook-bootstrap.sh`, `hook-output.sh`, `tool-input.sh` + `tool-input/*.py`, `hook-subproc-timeout.sh` | Resolve the host runtime (`claude`, `codex`, `cursor`, `opencode`, `pi`, `goose`, `hermes`) and its state dir; shared sourcing for delivery gates; emit host-correct hook JSON; parse tool payloads across hosts |
| Activation and safety | `sb-project-gate.sh`, `project-active.sh`, `jq-gate.sh`, `trivial-bypass.sh`, `nofollow-guard.sh`, `branch-scope.sh`, `plugin-cache-guard.sh`, `core-rules-integrity.sh` | Stay inert outside SB projects; jq-missing behaviour; legacy trivial bypass; refuse writes through symlinks (SEC-02); branch/worktree scoping; plugin-cache boundary; core-rules integrity pin |
| Skills and workflows | `required-skills.sh`, `skill-discovery.sh`, `workflow-utils.sh`, `quality-gates-mode.sh` | Default skill lists from the config template; installed-skill discovery; Flow Log row counting (single regex source); quality-gates mode |
| Delivery gates | `completion-audit/*.sh`, `doc-scheme-gate.sh`, `evidence-schema-gate.sh`, `artifact-substance-gate.sh`, `enterprise-policy.sh`, `github-run-list.sh` | Modules of `completion-audit.sh` (classification, planning tier, deploy tier, change class) and the delivery checks it runs |
| Orchestrator | `orchestrator-*.sh`, `agent-delegation-state.sh`, `review-fix-ladder-state.sh` | Parent-mode directives, flow queue, scheduler, event log, delegation and review-ladder state |
| Opt-in tools | `recommended-tools*.sh`, `graphify-gate.sh`, `agentmemory-gate.sh`, `rtk-gate.sh`, `context-mode-gate.sh`, `leanctx-gate.sh`, `alumnium-gate.sh`, `stack-compression-coordinator.sh` | Consent, install and usage gates for the five-tool stack and Alumnium |

### Skills

Every skill is a single `SKILL.md` file with YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`, optional `argument-hint`). The **composable flow skills** are orchestrators that sequence other skills:

- `silver-feature` — 20-step app development workflow
- `silver-ui` — UI variant of silver-feature, adds UI phase and review steps
- `silver-bugfix` — diagnosis-first bug fix workflow
- `silver-release` — cross-artifact review → deploy-checklist → ship ordering
- `silver-devops` — infrastructure / DevOps variant

Composable flow skills sequence SB-owned lifecycle skills. Legacy `gsd-*` marker names remain as compatibility aliases in hooks and config. After editing `skills/`, run `bash scripts/sync-codex-package.sh` to re-render `agents/claude/`, `host-bundles/{codex,cursor}/` and `plugins/silver-bullet/skill-source/`.

### Templates

`templates/` contains the files that `/sb:init` stamps into downstream projects:
- `silver-bullet.md.base` → becomes `silver-bullet.md` in the target project
- `silver-bullet.config.json.default` → default values for `.silver-bullet.json`
- `workflow.md.base` → becomes `.planning/workflows/<id>.md`
- `workflows/`, `doc-scheme.*.base`, `knowledge/`, `learnings/`, `CHANGELOG-project.md.base` and friends → workflow docs and the doc scheme

The project-instruction skeleton for Claude Code lives at `scripts/lib/install-claude/templates/CLAUDE.md.base`. It is an 18-line placeholder file, not a copy of this repo's `CLAUDE.md`.

**Critical invariant**: changes to enforcement logic (required skill lists, hook behavior) must be reflected in **both** `silver-bullet.md` (this repo's live copy) **and** `templates/silver-bullet.md.base` (the template stamped into new projects); `tests/scripts/test-silver-bullet-template-parity.sh` checks them. `docs/workflows/` must stay byte-identical to `templates/workflows/`.

### Tests

Tests use a consistent pattern:
- Each test runs against its own temporary directory (usually a real `git init` with a `.silver-bullet.json` and `silver-bullet.md`) and points `SILVER_BULLET_STATE_FILE` at a path under `${SB_RUNTIME_HOME_ROOT}/` (path validation in hooks rejects anything outside `${SB_RUNTIME_HOME_ROOT}/`). `tests/run-all-tests.sh` also gives every test file its own temporary `HOME` and `TMPDIR`.
- Hook scripts are invoked by piping JSON via stdin (matching the host hook protocol); `tests/lib/testlib.sh` provides helpers for new tests. Python unit tests live in `tests/python/` (`sbtest.load_module`), JavaScript/TypeScript tests in `tests/js/` (`node:test`).
- Results are parsed from `Results: N passed, M failed` lines.

---

## Key Invariants

- **`jq` is required** — `session-start` warns visibly when it is missing; most hooks then exit 0, but the core gates (`completion-audit.sh`, `dev-cycle-check.sh`, `forbidden-skill-check.sh`, `planning-file-guard.sh`, `uat-gate.sh`, `workflow-chain-guard.sh`) block in an initiated project (`hooks/lib/jq-gate.sh`). Never fail silently.
- **ERR trap pattern** — hooks install an `ERR` trap that exits 0 (some print a notice first) so unexpected failures don't block the runtime. Exceptions: `phase-archive.sh` fails closed (denies the `phases clear` it guards), and `rfl-policy-c-gate.sh` has no `ERR` trap.
- **Skill lists come from config** — required lists are read from `.silver-bullet.json`, falling back to `templates/silver-bullet.config.json.default` through `hooks/lib/required-skills.sh`. Remaining literals are deliberate fallbacks or fixed lists: `required-skills.sh` fallbacks for an unreadable template, the `finalization_skills` fallback and lifecycle exclusion list in `dev-cycle-check.sh`, the built-in forbidden list in `forbidden-skill-check.sh`, and the `REQUIRED_DEPLOY` fallback in `scripts/deploy-gate-snippet.sh` (CI compares it with the template).
- **Config is authoritative** — when `.silver-bullet.json` has `required_deploy`, it overrides the default; hooks never append extra mandatory skills on top
- **Plugin boundary** — `dev-cycle-check.sh` hard-blocks any Edit/Write targeting `${SB_RUNTIME_HOME_ROOT}/plugins/cache/**` (§8 enforcement)
- **State files must be under `${SB_RUNTIME_HOME_ROOT}/`** — `session-start` and `completion-audit.sh` reject `SILVER_BULLET_STATE_FILE` paths outside this prefix

## graphify

This project has a knowledge graph at graphify-out/ with god nodes, community structure, and cross-file relationships.

Rules:
- For codebase questions, first run `graphify query "<question>"` when graphify-out/graph.json exists. Use `graphify path "<A>" "<B>"` for relationships and `graphify explain "<concept>"` for focused concepts. These return a scoped subgraph, usually much smaller than GRAPH_REPORT.md or raw grep output.
- If graphify-out/wiki/index.md exists, use it for broad navigation instead of raw source browsing.
- Read graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md only for broad architecture review or when query/path/explain do not surface enough context.
- After modifying code, run `graphify update .` to keep the graph current (AST-only, no API cost).
